status: Linux 7.3.4 with 80 local Liuqin adaptations for Fedora, including changes shared with Recovery. CPU capacities and dynamic power coefficients use the OEM Cape descriptors; Liuqin CPU/LLCC BWMON nodes use mainline bindings with OEM bandwidth tables (Fedora temporary-boot verified on one Tianma unit: three CPU energy domains, PSCI idle accounting, both BWMON bindings and dynamic ICC votes; Recovery validation remains separate). Desktop boot arguments enable guarded 60/90/120/144 Hz switching for Tianma and CSOT; only Tianma has hardware evidence. Backlight probe uses default brightness and panel first-frame sequencing remains enabled. Exact image hardware validation is recorded separately. M81 fuel-gauge refresh follows the OEM periodic property-86 read, with frozen work during sleep and immediate refresh on resume. M81 charger property IDs and deferred vendor change events follow the shipping OEM module. Liuqin reads attached-source PDOs despite the missing UCSI capability flag; authentication uses their USB communication capability. UCSI decodes PPS request voltage/current and selected APDO limits, retaining M81 negotiated-power notifications for fresh RDO values. UCSI refreshes changed partner source capabilities without replacing the partner PD object, with bounded retries after transient registration failures. UCSI records registration only after a successful version read and clears freed connectors across firmware-service recovery. PMIC GLINK notification subscription and synchronous UCSI registration retry transient failures with bounded per-service budgets. Recovery rejects stale service results, drains work before client release, and resets asynchronous initialization state while cleaning partial ports before retry. UCSI GLINK validates complete read and write response lengths before accessing reply data. Liuqin USB-C DisplayPort keeps the OEM HBR2 ceiling and limits the lane count to the sink and the negotiated Type-C mux assignment. The MSM DP driver acknowledges a standalone PLL unlock during AUX idle without logging an AUX error. Liuqin connects the AudioReach DISPLAY_PORT_RX_0 backend to the MSM DP0 audio codec. MSM DP synchronously closes DPCM playback backends before link teardown and restores still-open frontends after the first DPU frame, independently of physical jack state. ALSA preparation and clocked audio MMIO are serialized; runtime route errors remain visible. Link-managed playback defers HDMI engine shutdown to component close, after CPU DAI shutdown has stopped its DSP graph; legacy/capture timing is unchanged. Four analog microphones use the OEM bias wiring, separate SoundWire master ports with OEM lanes/offsets and four-channel codec-DMA capture. TX mixer counts and mute cover all active decimators. Explicitly blocked display routes remain probeable without starting their backends; missing routes still fail. Four-channel Liuqin capture uses consecutive DSP channel identities to retain every physical microphone. WCD938x follows OEM TX-only codec IRQ ownership; status draining validates resources, read errors and bounded progress. Qualcomm SoundWire disables and drains its IRQ before gating the bus clock and reenables it after successful clock restoration. SoundWire v1.7 pairs the EE1 link manager with CPU1 FIFO registers and completion/error IRQ bits. WCD IRQ ownership, stop/start exclusion and v1.7 CPU1 FIFO changes were temporary-boot verified on one Liuqin unit: clean startup and eight runtime-PM cycles, repeated four-channel capture, software mute/volume and concurrent protected-speaker playback/capture. M81 retains the last valid battery readings only during transient transport loss and reports charging status as unknown, without hiding genuine zero or initial failures. Liuqin stops DSP graphs and SoundWire data ports before DAPM powers down during system suspend, and resets the playback queue during ALSA reprepare. ADSP service recovery preserves the PRM clock provider, rejects offline transport requests, restores votes and ordered device PM state, resets LPASS pins and SoundWire enumeration, and reinitializes WCD and microphone mixer state. Temporary-boot hardware checks on one Liuqin unit verify protected-speaker and four-channel capture recovery across s2idle, a controlled whole-ADSP restart, and s2idle after that restart, including actual audio and data progress. The diagnostic build enables PM_DEBUG and PM_SLEEP_DEBUG; runtime diagnostic output was disabled for the combined recovery checks. Transient errors during forced transport loss remain visible. Earlier kernels occasionally showed a GPIO46 wake interrupting sleep after boot or repeated recovery; its root cause was not confirmed; deep sleep, long-duration operation, external DP audio across sleep/restart, arbitrary firmware crashes and Recovery validation remain separate. Liuqin retains shared WCD ADC clocks until the final active input closes, uses OEM sample-rate-dependent analog HPF gate delays, and drains delayed unmute/filter work before shutdown or card removal. Offline capture teardown retires cached ADC/MICBIAS votes without accessing the volatile SoundWire bank-rate register. The fixed four-slot capture carrier keeps inactive slots clocked and muted while another input remains active. Temporary-boot checks verify single-input startup, partial ADC removal/restoration, rapid capture cycles, four-channel s2idle and controlled ADSP recovery, followed by release of capture clocks and bias enables. Liuqin retires STOP/CLOSE graph commands locally only when the owning GPR service is confirmed offline, including transport reset during a wait; host references and ports still close, and online failures remain visible. DPU physical cleanup clears stale software flush masks before assembling the current teardown, following the reviewed upstream fix; hardware reset, teardown updates and commit timeout checks remain enabled. Temporary-boot checks on one Tianma unit verify four-channel capture recovery through repeated controlled ADSP restarts and actual s2idle, plus 120 Hz display sleep/DPMS restoration with advancing frame counters and clear CTL/DSC flush registers. No APM STOP -102 or DPU commit timeout recurred in these short tests; arbitrary firmware crashes and long-duration display recovery remain separate. Nanosic handles GPIO46 status edges continuously while awake, following the OEM IRQ registration. The driver replaces the I2C dedicated wake handler with a managed ordinary wake IRQ, retaining system wake policy and data IRQ wakeup. Status IRQs perform no I2C or synthetic input; both suspend-time handlers honor disabled wake policy. Temporary-boot checks on one Liuqin unit confirm that GPIO46 is enabled and handles status edges while awake. First, rapid and post-key s2idle tests reach RTC wake; a Shift key wakes through the data IRQ, while disabled keyboard wake holds sleep until RTC. Driver unbind/rebind releases and reacquires both IRQs, followed by a verified Shift press/release and another RTC sleep. No early GPIO46 wake or IRQ ownership warning occurred in these checks; the prior intermittent cause and long-duration behavior remain unconfirmed. Installed-default normal-boot checks on the same unit confirm the matched module/topology set, four-channel desktop capture data, speaker calibration and silent playback progress, continuously enabled GPIO46 and RTC s2idle recovery. The project updater confirmed the new boot and restored disabled automatic writes; external DP audio was not retested during this default update. SM8475 uses the fixed OEM 13-point 220-900 MHz GPU table, GX and independent CX RPMh corners and ACD controls. A730 converts complete optional CX dependencies through cmd-db into GEN7 HFI entries; missing tables retain the legacy disabled value. GMU 200/500 MHz OPPs and the existing A730 bandwidth table already match the OEM. Temporary and installed-default normal boots on one Liuqin unit verify all 13 OPPs in both directions, a three-minute 900 MHz GLES load, automatic DVFS/runtime suspend, GLES render/compute readback, Turnip Vulkan, Rusticl GPU computation and four RTC s2idle recoveries. No GMU/IOMMU error occurred in these bounded checks. Analog voltage readback, thermal limiting, long-duration load, arbitrary GPU fault recovery, full OpenCL CTS and Recovery hardware validation remain separate. A730 preserves SP/TPL1 non-context bank modes in the IFPC/preemption restore list, matching OEM GEN7 behavior. Targeted image and rectangular-copy CTS, plus GLES render/compute readback, are verified on one unit; asynchronous strided-copy correctness requires the documented Fedora Mesa noearlypreamble workaround, and complete OpenCL conformance remains unverified. Liuqin A730 uses a bounded 5000 ms hangcheck interval for long desktop compute dispatches; hardware fault handling and progress retries remain enabled. Temporary and installed-default normal boots on one unit verify the default interval, long compute readback and subsequent GLES/OpenCL operation. A controlled non-progressing compute task verifies bounded hang detection and recovery. Full OpenCL conformance and Recovery hardware validation remain separate. Bonded video interfaces use a single CTL flush on active-CTL hardware while preserving both interface update bits. Executed driver-function regressions cover solo and bonded video on DPU 4 through 10, completion accounting and the old duplicate-flush path. Old/new/old kernel hardware comparison on one Tianma unit reproduces duplicate submissions and DSC flush timeouts only with the old callback. Temporary and installed-default normal boots pass short visible window/fullscreen rendering, four refresh rates, rotation, DPMS and RTC s2idle followed by explicit DPMS restore, with advancing interface frame counters and clear CTL/DSC flush registers; the user confirms picture and touch on the temporary boot. The project updater confirms the default kernel and restores disabled automatic writes. Matched modules and audio companions, four-channel capture data and the independent resume-display service are checked; new physical-key/lid and external DP audio tests are outside this display regression. Register logging amplifies the race window; normal-log rendering is checked separately. Long-duration behavior, other panels and Recovery hardware validation remain separate. Iris IRQ teardown drains the threaded handler outside the core lock before power-off. Empty/NOSHOW decoder outputs are recycled without dropping visible frames; error timestamps and source-change LAST markers are preserved. SM8450 uses OEM rate limits, per-frame reconstruction buffers and a dedicated CP_NON_PIXEL context for encoder ARP and page tables. Missing secure context retains decoder-only operation. Iris2 encoder drain accepts the OEM zero-flag acknowledgement while preserving real errors and strict handling on other platforms. Bounded module checks on one unit pass H.264/H.265 8-bit encoding at 854x480, 1280x720 and 1920x1080, default profiles, concurrent sessions and early-stop/reopen; complete encoded frame counts independently decode. H.264/H.265/VP9 720p decode matches all 60 software reference frame hashes. Host regressions cover ownership failure paths, drain acknowledgement flags and decoder buffer lifecycle. The complete kernel passes temporary-boot and installed-default normal-boot checks on one unit: both 720p encoders produce 60 decodable frames, all three decoders match 60 reference frame hashes, modules/audio companions and four-channel capture are verified, and the Fedora userland packages retain their official files. The temporary boot also covers all three encoder sizes, concurrent sessions, early-stop/reopen and idle RTC s2idle followed by new encode/decode sessions. No Iris/SMMU/GPU fault occurs in these bounded checks. The project updater confirms boot_a and the new boot generation, restores disabled automatic writes, and retains an off-device boot/store/companion backup. Long-duration operation, video sessions kept open across system sleep, 4K/10-bit/HDR, browser integration and Recovery hardware validation remain separate. Liuqin constrains the common USB controller to the shipping Gen1 ceiling with maximum-speed=super-speed; the existing DWC3 core owns the resulting device-speed and link settings. New image hardware validation is recorded separately. Liuqin UCSI obtains ordinary USB cable orientation from the serialized battery CC service before enabling USB roles. Hardware validation is recorded separately. Liuqin starts its DRD controller in peripheral mode until UCSI selects the first role after CC orientation, retaining the existing host fallback for later NONE requests. Liuqin prepares the initial ordinary-USB mux before the first role request, avoiding a late PHY mode reset during host training; existing partners and alternate-mode accessories retain their mux policy. SM8475 USB SerDes initialization includes the three omitted downstream VCO/core-clock/common registers and uses the matching V6 COM names. Liuqin defers connector publication and USB roles after failed lane preparation, retains acknowledged changes and retries fresh firmware state with bounded work canceled at suspend/removal. Liuqin connects all CPU temperature sensors to the three cpufreq cooling policies with 250 ms passive polling, retaining the existing trip temperatures and critical protection. Exact image hardware validation is recorded separately. M81 exposes acknowledged 0..15 host thermal levels, USB input-current votes, raw thermal telemetry and a charging cooling device. Liuqin ADC7 thermistor channels follow the OEM board wiring; exact image hardware validation is recorded separately. Liuqin retains only the ADSP charger diagnostic transport across local driver unbind, drains client callbacks, reuses intents and preserves remote-close and edge-removal cleanup. Exact image hardware validation is recorded separately. Front-module EEPROM is a read-only IMX596-owned NVMEM provider, with full sensor runtime PM and serialization against streaming; the independent at24 node stays disabled. GMU OOB tracing records request result and duration without extending the handshake timeout. Failed GPU initialization clears its OOB request; timestamp queries propagate runtime resume failures. Opt-in IFE680 NV12 supports the two front binned RAW10 geometries and all Bayer orientations, with hardware demosaic, black-preserving white balance, calibrated lens shading, black-level subtraction, sRGB gamma and full-range BT.601 conversion. A fixed-shape local ABI exposes frame-numbered Bayer grid statistics, Q10 red/blue gains and a stopped-stream-only 17x13 shading mesh. Paired libcamera implements basic automatic exposure/white balance and per-module calibration. Full OEM IQ, frame-exact request controls and general-purpose ISP support remain outside this experimental path. Exact image hardware validation is recorded separately. CC131 colour correction adds a bounded RGB Q10 matrix control; paired libcamera applies the stock front IPE D50 baseline before IFE gamma. IPE TF21 single-pass temporal filtering is available through the separately prepared experimental bridge; multi-exposure HDR is not implemented. Rear S5KJN1 binned RAW10 uses the IFE680 NV12 path through IQ ABI 2. Contiguous NV12 allocations include chroma beyond the old PIX byte limit. The wide colour matrix control selects Q9 when stock warm-light coefficients exceed Q10 signed-12-bit range; front calibration is disabled for rear geometry. IPE processing remains a separately prepared experimental bridge. Rear S5KJN1 exposes read-only sensor-owned EEPROM with streaming exclusion; paired libcamera applies checked per-unit WB, AF bounds and geometry-bound LSC. CAMSS closes the buffer-completion gate atomically at stop, preventing late-IRQ active-count underflow on restart. CAMSS unwinds only subdevices that accepted stream start when a later subdevice fails, preventing stale active outputs after sensor errors. GMU HFI tracing records command/response queue indices and interrupt state. The fault IRQ only acknowledges CM3_FAULT, preserving the sender-owned response notification; response consumers order payload reads after observing the firmware producer index. These fix notification ownership and DMA ordering gaps without extending timeouts; the historical first timeout has not been reproduced. The rear S5KJN1 has a PM8350C software-strobed V4L2 flash subdevice and LED-class torch. The rear Q-Tech S5KJN1 exposes its four OEM readouts; IFE680 PIX supports the three binned geometries. The SM8450 H.264 encoder constrains the level to the negotiated picture size and frame rate.
